data.title: Nipple eczema — viva
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Nipple eczema** (Eczemas)_

**Q1. What are the causes of nipple/areolar eczema?**
- Atopic dermatitis (minor criterion of Hanifin–Rajka) — commonest, usually bilateral, adolescent girls
- Irritant (friction — 'jogger's nipple', breastfeeding — saliva, pumps), allergic contact (nursing creams, lanolin, fragrances, bra materials), Candida during breastfeeding, scabies (areolae in women), seborrhoeic

**Q2. Why is unilateral persistent nipple eczema a red flag?**
- Paget's disease of the nipple — intra-epidermal spread of underlying ductal breast carcinoma; unilateral, slowly progressive, well-defined, crusted/eroded, may have nipple retraction, discharge, lump
- Any unilateral nipple eczema not responding to 3–4 weeks of topical steroid needs biopsy and breast imaging

**Q3. Differentiate eczema from Paget's disease of nipple.**
- Eczema: bilateral, itchy, ill-defined, starts on areola, fluctuates, responds to steroids, nipple intact
- Paget's: unilateral, little itch, sharply demarcated, starts on nipple then areola, persistent, steroid-unresponsive, nipple may be destroyed/retracted; histology — large pale Paget cells (CK7+, CEA+, HER2+)

**Q4. Other differentials.**
- Psoriasis, erosive adenomatosis of nipple, Bowen's disease, hyperkeratosis of nipple and areola (naevoid), tinea, herpes, scabies

**Q5. Management of nipple eczema in breastfeeding women.**
- Emollient (pure petrolatum), mild topical steroid applied after feeds and wiped before the next feed; treat Candida in mother and baby (oral thrush) with topical azole/nystatin; correct latch; avoid allergenic nursing creams

**Q6. Work-up in a non-healing case.**
- Patch test (if contact allergy), KOH, skin biopsy, mammography/ultrasound for Paget's

**Q7. What is hyperkeratosis of nipple and areola?**
- Rare benign verrucous thickening and pigmentation — naevoid, associated with ichthyosis/AD/ CTCL or oestrogen therapy; keratolytics, retinoids, cryotherapy

## Quick spotter facts
- Unilateral, steroid-resistant nipple 'eczema' — biopsy for Paget's disease

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Eczemas, breast dermatoses). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
